_comment: Lightning 2.0 Phase 4, the population and liquidity engine. fn_cash_cluster_live_eligible is the one predicate the specification asks for: how many PLAYERS Lightning could deal to in a Cluster right now. It is NOT the board count - that question is how many players are in this game, it counts a sitting-out, busted or leaving player because all three are in the game, and tests/one-definition-of-a-games-players.law.test.ts pins it across three readers. The table predicate here is fn_cash_cluster_census's byte for byte so the two can never disagree about which tables belong to the game; only the seat predicate is narrower, and a horse counts exactly like a human (Law 10.5, pinned twice in server/src/cluster). One count(DISTINCT) over a UNION of the seated and pooled halves, because those halves are not disjoint in the window a Phase 5 conversion opens. fn_cash_cluster_population is the same number with its breakdown, which deliberately does not sum: the exclusion categories overlap, an empty chair is in none of them, and the answer says so in a field of its own. Four of the specification's thirteen categories - disconnected, expired disconnect, ghost BB and watching - have no representation in PostgreSQL at all and are named in every answer rather than rounded off; p_disconnected is the seam spec Phase 14 fills. fn_cash_cluster_lightning_thresholds is the only place the four mandated numbers are written (6-max ON 18 OFF 12, full ring 27 and 18), read from cash_games.ruleset_snapshot -> lightning when it names them, with the hysteresis rule enforced rather than trusted and an invalid configuration refused in favour of the defaults rather than raised, because it is read on a path a tick takes. fn_cash_cluster_pool_health is one Cluster's liquidity in one shape. The existing fn_cash_cluster_lightning_state gains thresholds and a descriptive verdict and reads the SCALAR, not the breakdown, because fn_cash_game_lobby embeds it. Nothing here converts anything: that is Phase 5.
